items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: Luke Smith was working with me. Luke Smith, Luke Smith and I were good friends.

ctx.x: We went in Connie's Inn. Well, there was something different for me, too. Uptown and all, Connie's Inn, strictly white, no colored. It was nice, very nice, very nice. See, they -- Connie, he was the playboy, but George, his brother, he was the businessman. George came to us and said, listen, fellows, says, we're not going to have anybody here tonight. It's sold out to Dutch Schultze. Lord, lord, lord. (Unintelligible) I was scared to death. Dutch Schultz was the biggest gangster in town at that time.

He and his men had rented Connie's Inn. And, lord, to tell the truth, I didn't feel like I could play or nothing. I was scared to death. And I was talking to the fellow next to me, Luke Smith was working with me. Luke Smith, Luke Smith and I were good friends. He was Joe Smith's brother. Luke could play better trumpet than any of the other two. He was the best. But you wouldn't think he did it, because he liked to play pool so much.
Luke was in __________ band, Luke and I were great friends. Luke says, I ain't paying him any mind. I said, why? He says, well, they treat you nice. It'll be all right.
